candidates.name: Thames Barrier
candidates.story: Engineers used gates that rotate up from the riverbed to block storm surges while leaving navigation spans clear when open. The barrier became operational in 1982 and officially opened in 1984.
candidates.art_direction: Show a raised steel gate between two of the silver piers from a low river viewpoint so the gate profile is visible.

candidates.name: Landwasser Viaduct
candidates.story: The three tallest masonry piers rose without external scaffold towers. Iron frames were embedded in the piers and raised with the work; cross beams between them carried electric lifting cranes that delivered stone to the growing pier tops. The completed limestone viaduct was finished in October 1902. This year denotes bridge completion, not the later opening of railway service.
candidates.art_direction: Depict the tall piers under construction in 1901–1902, with embedded iron frames projecting above masonry and cross beams carrying the electric lifting equipment. Use owner archive photographs and contemporary drawings to establish the exact geometry before artwork. Show the curved alignment toward the rock-face tunnel, five piers and eventual six arches only at a stage supported by records. The no-external-scaffolding claim applies to the tall piers: any arches under construction must have historically supported centering. Keep the cranes and a lifted stone load legible at wall distance and in grayscale, with quiet upper-right space in independently composed Frame orientations. Do not draw modern tower cranes or a completed train running through unfinished arches. Confirm the line-opening and first-service milestones separately before final live copy.

candidates.name: Centre Pompidou
candidates.story: Cast-steel gerberettes pivoted at the exterior columns and supported the long-span floor beams, working with exterior tension rods to keep the exhibition floors open. Peter Rice chose cast steel for these sculptural connectors; after an initial test failure, specialist heat treatment helped resolve the fracture problem. The completed building dates to 1977. The owner’s chronology separately records completion of the steel frame on 20 June 1975, inauguration on 31 January 1977 and opening to the public on 2 February 1977.
candidates.art_direction: Reconstruct installation of one cast-steel gerberette around 1974–1975. Make the pinned column connection, beam bearing and outboard tension-rod connection legible, with repeated exposed portal frames behind. Use owner archive photographs, the architect’s drawings and the Arup collection to establish the actual casting profile, erection sequence, sling arrangement and crane type before artwork. Distinguish cast-steel arms from welded girders; do not show the original rejected competition truss detail as built. Compose landscape and portrait independently, retain quiet upper-right caption areas and preserve connector silhouettes in grayscale. This construction angle concerns casting, testing and structural load transfer, distinct from a general museum or closure story in any sibling recipe.
